definition: Evolutionary developmental robotics (evo-devo-robo for short) refers to methodologies that systematically integrate evolutionary robotics, epigenetic robotics and morphogenetic robotics to study the evolution, physical and mental development and learning of natural intelligent systems in robotic systems.
details: The field was formally suggested and fully discussed in a published paper and further discussed in a published dialogue. The theoretical foundation of evo-devo-robo includes evolutionary developmental biology (evo-devo), evolutionary developmental psychology, developmental cognitive neuroscience etc. Further discussions on evolution, development and learning in robotics and design can be found in a number of papers, including papers on hardware systems and computing tissues.

explainer.lead: Evolutionary developmental robotics looks at intelligent machines through three linked processes: change across generations, development of body and mind, and learning during a lifetime. Combining them lets researchers ask not just which robot performs best, but how its abilities emerge and grow.

tiers.eli5: Imagine making toy robots over many generations, but not treating each one as finished the moment it is built. Each robot grows its body and abilities, then practices tasks and learns; what happens helps shape the next generation. This lets researchers explore how growing up, practicing, and passing on designs work together.
tiers.practitioner: In practice, researchers specify how inherited designs change across generations, how a robot's body and control develop, and how learning modifies its abilities during operation. Robotic hardware and computing tissues are among the settings discussed for this work. A key pitfall is conflating learning within one robot's lifetime with inherited change between generations, or changing morphology and control without examining their interaction.
tiers.paperLevel: Evo-devo-robo = methodologies integrating evolutionary robotics, epigenetic robotics, and morphogenetic robotics to study evolution, physical and mental development, and learning of natural intelligent systems in robotic systems. Its theoretical foundations include evolutionary developmental biology, evolutionary developmental psychology, and developmental cognitive neuroscience. It is an umbrella research framework rather than a single fixed algorithm, so an experiment must specify how these processes interact.

explainer.example: Consider a population of small walking robots. Over generations, their inherited body-and-controller designs vary; after each robot is built, its control develops and it then improves its walking through practice. Researchers compare the robots to see whether development and learning change which designs succeed, rather than judging every design only by an initial, fully formed controller.

usedIn.name: Evolutionary robotics
usedIn.detail: Contributes methods for studying change in robotic systems across generations.

usedIn.name: Epigenetic robotics
usedIn.detail: Contributes the study of development as robots acquire physical and mental capabilities.

usedIn.name: Morphogenetic robotics
usedIn.detail: Contributes a focus on the development of robotic bodies and their organization.

usedIn.name: Hardware systems and computing tissues
usedIn.detail: Provide settings for further work on evolution, development, and learning in robotics and design.

explainer.intuition: A robot's abilities need not be treated as fixed at birth or designed all at once. Evo-devo-robo brings inherited change, growth, and learning into one research programme so their interactions can be studied in robotic systems.
howItWorks: Begin with robotic systems whose inherited designs can change across generations.
Allow each robot's body and mental capabilities to develop rather than treating them as fully fixed.
Let learning alter the robot's abilities during its lifetime.
Study how evolution, development, and learning affect one another and the resulting intelligent behaviour.
explainer.whyItMatters: It provides a common framework for studying processes that are often examined separately. That can reveal how a robot's lifetime development and learning interact with longer-term evolutionary change.
misconceptions: It is not just evolutionary optimization of a finished robot: development and learning are central too.
It is not one specific algorithm, but a family of methodologies integrating several research approaches.
Learning within a robot's lifetime is not the same as evolutionary change between generations.

diagram.caption: Evo-devo-robo studies the interactions among inherited change, development, and lifetime learning rather than treating them as isolated processes.
